title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Make polite requests, ask favours, invite and be invited, accept and refuse gracefully, and address people respectfully.
intro:
Courtesy (**ادب**) and hospitality are at the heart of Pashtun culture. Invitations are pressed warmly and refused politely at first; requests are softened with 'if it's no trouble'; and blessings — 'may God keep you', 'may you live long' — are woven into everyday speech.

In this unit you'll learn the language of politeness: soft requests ('could you …?'), the **optative** 'may … / let …' with دې, and the **vocative** forms used to call and address people.

vocab.note: m. زحمت مه کوئ 'don't trouble yourself'.
Present stem بول-: بولم bóləm. Perfective: وبولم.
f. هيله کوم 'I request / I hope'.
m. ستاسو په خدمت کې 'at your service'.
Invariable. Said when shown great kindness.
ستاسو منندوی يم 'I'm grateful to you'.
f. خپله. Refers back to the subject: خپل کور 'his own house'.
ستا قربان شم 'I'd give my life for you' — affectionate, often from elders.

phrases.native: کولای شئ چې ما سره کومک وکړئ؟
phrases.roman: kawə́lāy shəy che mā sara kumák wə́kṛəy?

phrases.native: که زحمت نه وي، دروازه بنده کړئ.
phrases.roman: ka zahmát na wi, darwā́za bánda kṛəy.
phrases.en: If it's no trouble, please close the door.
Yes, of course! Please come and sit.

phrases.native: نن ماښام زموږ کور ته راشئ.
phrases.roman: nən māṣā́m zmuẓ kor ta rā́shəy.
phrases.en: Come to our house this evening.

phrases.native: ډېره مننه، خو نن نه شم راتلای.
phrases.roman: ḍéra manə́na, xo nən na shəm rātlā́y.
phrases.en: Thank you very much, but I can't come today.
Please don't go to any trouble.
Have some more — don't be shy!

phrases.note: In eastern/Peshawar speech also يئ yəy.

phrases.en: May you see it grow! (said to new parents)
phrases.note: A blessing, lit. 'may you see (him/her) grow up'.

grammar.title: Soft requests: 'could you …?', 'if it's no trouble'
grammar.body:
A bare imperative can sound abrupt, so Pashto softens requests in several ways:

1. **Polite imperative** with -əy and مهرباني وکړئ / لطفاً: لطفاً کېنئ 'please sit'.
2. **کولای شئ چې … ؟** 'can you …?' + subjunctive: کولای شئ چې ورو خبرې وکړئ؟ 'could you speak slowly?'
3. **کېدای شي چې … ؟** 'is it possible that …?': کېدای شي چې يو ګيلاس اوبه راکړئ؟ 'could I have a glass of water?'
4. **که زحمت نه وي** 'if it isn't any trouble' before the request.
5. **اجازه ده چې … ؟** 'is there permission that …?' for 'may I …?'

To **refuse** gracefully, thank first and give a reason: ډېره مننه، خو … 'thank you very much, but …'. To **insist** (a host's duty!): خامخا راشئ 'you simply must come'.

examples.native: کېدای شي چې ستاسو ټيلفون وکاروم؟
examples.roman: kedā́y shi che stāso ṭelifún wə́kārawəm?

examples.native: کولای شئ چې دا ما ته ووايئ؟
examples.roman: kawə́lāy shəy che dā mā ta wə́wāyəy?

examples.native: که زحمت نه وي، ما ته يوه ټکسي ونيسئ.
examples.roman: ka zahmát na wi, mā ta yáwa ṭaksí wə́nisəy.
examples.en: If it's no trouble, get a taxi for me.

examples.native: ډېره مننه، خو زه بايد کور ته لاړ شم.
examples.roman: ḍéra manə́na, xo zə bāyád kor ta lāṛ shəm.
examples.en: Thank you very much, but I must go home.

grammar.title: Wishes and 'let …': the optative with دې
grammar.body:
The particle **دې** (de, unstressed — not the same as the clitic 'your') + a present verb expresses a **wish, blessing or third-person command**: 'may …', 'let …'.

**Blessings**: خدای **دې** خير درکړي 'may God give you good', ژوندی **دې** وي 'long may he live', کور **دې** ودان وي 'may your house prosper', ستړی **دې** نه شې 'may you not be tired'.
**Let him/her**: هغه **دې** راشي 'let him come', ماشومان **دې** لوبې وکړي 'let the children play'.

For 'let's …' use **راځئ چې** + 1st person plural subjunctive: راځئ چې ډوډۍ وخورو 'let's eat'.

grammar.title: Addressing people: the vocative
grammar.body:
When you call or address someone directly, Pashto nouns take the **vocative** form. Masculine nouns usually add **-a**, feminine nouns **-e**:

ورور → **وروره** wróra! 'brother!'
زوی → **زويه** zóya! 'son!'
خدای → **خدايه** xudā́ya! 'O God!'
خور → **خورې** xóre! 'sister!'
لور → **لورې** lúre! 'daughter!'
Names do it too: احمده! ahmáda, ګلالۍ → ګلالۍ! (unchanged).

Respectful address: elders are called **حاجي صاحب**, **ماما** (uncle), **ادې** or **مور جانې** (mother), **کاکا**, **ترور**; teachers **استاد**; officials **ښاغلی / صاحب**. Adding **جانه / جانې** ('dear') makes any name warm and affectionate.

dialogue.title: An invitation to dinner
dialogue.setting: Gul Agha meets his new neighbour, Daniel, and invites him home.

lines.speaker: Gul Agha
lines.native: دانيال جانه، نن ماښام زموږ کور ته راشه، ډوډۍ به سره وخورو.
lines.roman: dāniyā́l jā́na, nən māṣā́m zmuẓ kor ta rā́sha, ḍoḍə́y ba sara wə́xwru.
lines.en: Dear Daniel, come to our house this evening — we'll eat together.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.native: ډېره مننه، خو زحمت مه کوئ.
lines.roman: ḍéra manə́na, xo zahmát ma kawə́y.
lines.en: Thank you very much, but please don't go to any trouble.

lines.speaker: Gul Agha
lines.native: زحمت څه دی؟ ته زموږ مېلمه يې. خامخا راشه!
lines.roman: zahmát tsə day? tə zmuẓ melmə́ ye. xāmaxā́ rā́sha!
lines.en: What trouble? You're our guest. You must come!

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.native: سمه ده، ضرور به راشم. په څو بجو؟
lines.roman: sáma da, zarúr ba rā́shəm. pə tso bajó?
lines.en: All right, I'll certainly come. At what time?

lines.speaker: Gul Agha
lines.native: د ماښام له لمانځه وروسته، اووه بجې.
lines.roman: də māṣā́m la lmā́ndza wrústa, owə́ báje.
lines.en: After the evening prayer — seven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.native: السلام عليکم! دا د ماشومانو لپاره يوه وړه ډالۍ ده.
lines.roman: assalā́mu ʿaláykum! dā də māshumā́no lapā́ra yáwa wáṛa ḍālə́y da.
lines.en: (That evening) Hello! This is a little gift for the children.

lines.speaker: Gul Agha
lines.native: ولې دې زحمت وکړ! تشريف راوړه، کېنه.
lines.roman: wə́le de zahmát wə́kaṛ! tashríf rā́wṛa, kéna.
lines.en: Why did you go to the trouble! Please come in, sit down.

lines.speaker: Gul Agha
lines.native: نور وخوره، شرم مه کوه! دا کور ستا خپل کور دی.
lines.roman: nor wə́xwra, sharm ma kawa! dā kor stā xpəl kor day.
lines.en: Have some more, don't be shy! This house is your own house.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.native: مننه، ډېر ماړه شوم. تاسو ډېر مهربان ياست، زه شرمنده يم.
lines.roman: manə́na, ḍer mā́ṛa shwəm. tāso ḍer mehrabā́n yāst, zə sharmindá yəm.
lines.en: Thank you, I'm really full. You're very kind — I'm overwhelmed.

lines.speaker: Gul Agha
lines.native: ستړی مه شې! بيا هم راځه.
lines.roman: stə́ṛay ma she! biyā́ ham rā́dza.
lines.en: Thank you for coming! Do come again.

culture: **Melmastia** (مېلمستيا, hospitality) is one of the core values of *Pashtunwali*, the traditional Pashtun code alongside honour (ننګ، عزت), courage and **nanawatai** (ننواتې, giving refuge to anyone who asks). A guest is treated as a gift from God: the host serves the best food, insists you eat more, and may walk you to the end of the lane when you leave. It's polite to decline once or twice before accepting an invitation, to bring a small gift (sweets, fruit, something for the children), and to remove your shoes. Expect to be offered the place of honour; the host may not eat until you have. Thank your host with blessings rather than just مننه: کور دې ودان، خدای دې خير درکړي.
